channel.title: Robot Dictionary, new entries
channel.description: New robots added to the Robot Dictionary.

item.title: 2-XL
item.description: Talking educational toy robot sold by Mego from 1978 to 1981 and by Tiger Electronics from 1992 to 1995, regarded as the first smart toy.

item.title: 5DX
item.description: Automated inspection robot, made by Hewlett Packard and later Agilent Technologies, that took 3D radiographic images of assembled circuit boards to check the solder.

item.title: 8A4 class ROUV
item.description: Remotely operated underwater vehicle of the work class type, developed by China's Shenyang Institute of Automation for jobs ranging from oil platform servicing to salvage and rescue.

item.title: ABISMO
item.description: Japanese deep sea remotely operated vehicle built by the Japan Agency for Marine-Earth Science and Technology as the replacement for Kaikō, which was lost in 2003.

item.title: ACM III
item.description: Snake robot built by Shigeo Hirose, among the first machines to crawl by undulating its body like a real snake.

item.title: Actroid
item.description: Highly lifelike android created at Osaka University and produced by Kokoro, usually given the appearance of a young Japanese woman.

item.title: Adelbrecht
item.description: Ball shaped robot that could talk and interact with people, designed by Martin Spanjaard.

item.title: Aerones
item.description: Rope suspended robotic system that climbs wind turbine blades to clean, inspect, test lightning conductors and repair leading edges.

item.title: AESOP
item.description: Robotic arm that held and moved the endoscope camera during keyhole surgery, the first surgical robot cleared by the US Food and Drug Administration.

item.title: Affetto
item.description: Research robot developed at the University of Osaka in Japan, first built in 2012.

item.title: Agile ONE
item.description: Humanoid robot introduced in 2025 by Agile Robots, a robotics company from Germany.

item.title: AI Suitcase
item.description: Navigation robot in the form of a suitcase that guides people with visual impairments, developed in 2021 as part of a museum artificial intelligence project.

item.title: Ai-Da
item.description: Humanoid robot artist, completed in 2019 by Engineered Arts, that produces drawings, paintings and sculptures.

item.title: AIBO ERS-7
item.description: Consumer entertainment robot in Sony's AIBO series, released in 2003 as the first model the company explicitly presented as a dog.

item.title: Aiko Chihira
item.description: Humanoid android from Toshiba that greeted shoppers as a receptionist at a Mitsukoshi department store in Tokyo.

item.title: Air-Cobot
item.description: Wheeled collaborative robot from a French research project, built to check aircraft during maintenance while working alongside human staff.

item.title: AISoy1
item.description: Consumer pet robot from Spain's AISoy Robotics, counted among the first with emotional learning, whose decisions weigh logical and emotional factors rather than fixed replies.

item.title: Ajeeb
item.description: Fake chess automaton built by cabinet maker Charles Hooper, which appeared to play on its own while a skilled human player hidden inside made the moves.

item.title: Albert HUBO
item.description: Walking humanoid robot that mounts a head on a full size two legged frame, based on the HUBO biped from the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology.

item.title: Alice
item.description: Tiny cube shaped mobile robot measuring 2 by 2 by 2 cm, created at the Autonomous Systems Lab of the École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne.

item.title: Allen
item.description: Wheeled research robot that Rodney Brooks's group built in the late 1980s, the first they based on the subsumption architecture.

item.title: AMOR
item.description: Autonomous robot built for outdoor operation at the University of Siegen in Germany, working without direct human control.

item.title: Andromeda
item.description: Surgical robot developed to carry out parts of procedures autonomously rather than only extending a surgeon's hands.

item.title: Andy Warhol Robot
item.description: Animatronic figure of Andy Warhol that the artist created in 1981 to serve as a self portrait.

item.title: Aoi Erika
item.description: Android announcer created for the television network Nippon TV, introduced in 2017 and standing 166 cm tall.

item.title: Aquanaut
item.description: Underwater robot that cruises as an autonomous vehicle and then opens into a two armed remotely operated vehicle at its work site.

item.title: Arachno-Bot
item.description: Eight legged spider inspired robot developed in 2011 at the Fraunhofer Institute of Manufacturing Engineering and Automation in Stuttgart to survey areas too dangerous for people.

item.title: Archie
item.description: Teen sized humanoid robot over 120 cm tall, developed from 2004 by TU Wien in Austria and the University of Manitoba in Canada.

item.title: Argo
item.description: Uncrewed camera sled towed deep underwater, developed by Robert Ballard at Woods Hole's Deep Submergence Laboratory, that helped find the wreck of the Titanic in 1985.

item.title: Argus
item.description: Robotic camera platform from MIT's City Scanning project that captured omnidirectional images tagged with their geographic position, dating from 1990.

item.title: Armatron
item.description: Joystick controlled toy robot arm from Tomy, sold through Radio Shack stores in the United States from 1984, with no automatic functions.

item.title: ARTOS
item.description: Autonomous robot for transport and service tasks, developed at the University of Kaiserslautern in Germany.

item.title: Aseon Pod
item.description: Robotic micro depot that charges, cleans and services self driving cars between trips.

item.title: Astrobee
item.description: System of three cube shaped free flying robots from NASA's Ames Research Center that helps astronauts with routine chores aboard the International Space Station.

item.title: Asuro
item.description: Programmable robot able to act autonomously, carrying out behaviours that its user writes and loads as software.

item.title: Atalante
item.description: Self balancing exoskeleton from Wandercraft that lets people with paralysis walk without crutches.

item.title: Audi Lunar Quattro
item.description: Small German lunar rover developed in 2015 by engineers of the PTScientists team, with backing from Audi and partners in several countries.

item.title: Autonomous Benthic Explorer
item.description: Autonomous underwater vehicle operated by the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution that surveyed broad stretches of seabed down to 4500 m until its loss at sea in 2010.

item.title: Autonomous Shipboard Humanoid
item.description: Humanoid robot developed at the United States Naval Research Laboratory with Virginia Tech and the University of Pennsylvania to move around ships, climb ladders and fight fires.

item.title: AutoPallet
item.description: Swarm of small mobile robots that move cardboard boxes and install into existing warehouses.

item.title: AUV ABYSS
item.description: REMUS 6000 autonomous underwater vehicle built by Hydroid in 2008 and owned by GEOMAR, used to map the deep seabed and gather data from the water column.

item.title: AUV-150
item.description: Indian autonomous underwater vehicle under development by scientists at the Central Mechanical Engineering Research Institute in Durgapur, West Bengal, with support from IIT Kharagpur.

item.title: Ava 500
item.description: Autonomous office telepresence robot from iRobot that drove itself to a chosen meeting room, using video equipment from Cisco.

item.title: Avadin
item.description: Care robot for older people developed by the South Korean company Wonderful Platform, also known by the name Dasom.

item.title: Axle Robot Kit
item.description: Robot kit from the American company True Robotics that students in grades 6 to 8 build for classroom learning.

item.title: Azalea
item.description: Robots that load and sort checked luggage in airport baggage halls.

item.title: Banryu
item.description: Robot product model developed in Japan and manufactured by the electronics company Sanyo.

item.title: Baxter
item.description: Two armed collaborative industrial robot from Rethink Robotics, the startup founded by Rodney Brooks, that has an animated face.

item.title: BB-8 by Sphero
item.description: App controlled rolling toy modelled on the droid from the 2015 Star Wars film, a ball with a magnetically held head.

item.title: Bear Flag autonomous tractor
item.description: Retrofit kit that turned existing farm tractors and implements into driverless machines; the company was acquired by Deere.
